div.head: II As 10.1
div.ab: Gif mon ðonne onfinde, þæt heora ænig on fore gewitnysse sy, þæt his gewitnysse næfre eft nawht ne forstande; ⁊ gesylle eac XXX scill. to wite.
Be wore gewitnesse. Gif mon þonne afinde, þæt heora ænig on wore gewitnesse wære, þæt næfre his gewitnes eft noht ne forstonde; ⁊ eac gesylle XXX scll' to wite.
Gif man þonne onfinde, þæt heora ænig on wore [gewitnesse sie], þæt his gewitnes næfre eft nauht ne forst[ande]; ⁊ geselle eac XXX scill' to wite.
Si autem pernoscatur, quod eorum aliquis in falso testimonio sit, eius testimonium deinceps numquam prestet aliquid; et etiam emendet XXX sol. (et habeat dominus illam cambitionem).
Be wore gewitnesse. Gif mon þonne afinde, þæt heora ænig on wore gewitnesse wære, þæt næfre his gewitnes eft noht ne forstonde; ⁊ eac gesylle XXX scll' to wite.
But if it is found that any one of them has borne false witness, never again shall his witness be valid; and moreover he shall pay a fine of 30 shillings.
Concerning false witness. If it is then discovered that any of them gave false witness, his witness is never again to be valid; and also he is to pay 30 shillings as a fine.

(Über falsches Zeugniss. H) Wenn man aber herausfindet, dass einer von jenen in falschem Zeugniss gewesen ist: dass niemals wieder sein Zeugniss etwas gelte; und er zahle auch [dem König] 30 Schill. zur Strafe.
(On false witness. H) But if it is found out that any of them has been in false witness: that his witness shall never again count for anything; and let him also pay [the king] 30 shillings as a fine.
div.note: Ld's ‘on fore’ for ‘on wore’ (false); Liebermann thinks Ot and Ld's ‘onfinde’ more original than H's ‘afinde’.
